title: Isolation-based Spherical Ensemble Representations for Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Unsupervised tabular anomaly detection suffers from conflicting distributional assumptions, quadratic complexity and weak handling of local anomalies; ISER addresses this by sampling psi-point subsets, building hyperspheres whose nearest-neighbour radii act as a monotonic proxy for local density, and encoding every point as a t-dimensional ensemble representation (phi = 1 - 1/r when covered, phi = 1 otherwise). Two scores are derived from that representation - the arithmetic mean (ISER-A) and the cosine similarity to the all-ones anomaly reference (ISER-S) - and the same representation is reused as a transformed feature space for an inverted-path-length Isolation Forest (ISER-IF). Averaged over 5 runs on 20 real-world datasets, ISER-S reaches the best average AUC-ROC of 0.8523 (ISER-A 0.8399) against 12 baselines, and ISER-IF improves iForest on all nine datasets in Table IV, e.g. 0.8530 -> 0.9314 on Ionosphere.

match_target.why: This is exactly the row the user asked for (Table IV, ISER-IF, Ionosphere) and Ionosphere is by far the cheapest dataset in that table (351 samples, 32 features, 126 anomalies), so the full pipeline (psi-point sampling, nearest-neighbour radii, phi-space encoding, inverted iForest scoring) can be verified in minutes on CPU while still demonstrating ISER's central contribution that the ensemble representation lifts Isolation Forest.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUC-ROC is a bounded score on a small evaluation set (Ionosphere, 351 points, below the 2,000-example threshold of rule 2) and the paper reports only the mean of 5 runs, no std or CI, so the band is 2.0 points = 0.02 in the fraction scale the paper prints (rule 1 does not apply because no spread is given).

requirements.stmt: For each of the t partitionings, independently sample psi points from the dataset without replacement; every sampled point becomes a hypersphere centre.
requirements.quote: For each partitioning Hi, we begin by randomly sampling a subset Di ⊂D of size ψ without replacement

requirements.stmt: The radius of a hypersphere centred at z is the distance from z to its nearest neighbour inside the same sampled subset Di (excluding z itself).
requirements.cite: Section III-A, radius definition; Algorithm 1, line 5
requirements.quote: The radius of this hypersphere is determined by the distance between z and its nearest neighbor in Di \ {z}

requirements.stmt: For a query point x, find all hyperspheres of partition Hi that cover x and keep the one with the smallest radius; this is the covering hypersphere used for x.
requirements.quote: we select the covering hypersphere with the smallest radius

requirements.stmt: Encode phi_i(x) = 1 - 1/r[zhat_i(x)] when x is covered by at least one hypersphere of Hi, and phi_i(x) = 1 when it is covered by none.
requirements.cite: Section III-A, phi definition; Algorithm 1, lines 13-16
requirements.quote: we assign φi(x) = 1, indicating that the point is not covered by any hyperspheres in this partitioning

requirements.stmt: The ensemble representation of a point is the t-dimensional concatenation of its per-partitioning phi values.
requirements.quote: The ensemble representation of point x is constructed by concatenating the coverage indicators from all t partitionings

requirements.stmt: ISER-A scores a point by the arithmetic mean of its ensemble representation components (higher = more anomalous).
requirements.cite: Section III-B, Average-based Scoring; Algorithm 1, line 20
requirements.quote: The average-based anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean of all ensemble components, effectively measuring the average degree of isolation across all partitionings

requirements.stmt: ISER-S scores a point by the cosine similarity between its ensemble representation and the all-ones anomaly reference vector 1 in R^t.
requirements.cite: Section III-B, Similarity-based Scoring; Algorithm 1, line 21
requirements.quote: The similarity-based anomaly score is computed using cosine similarity between the point’s ensemble representation and the anomaly reference vector

requirements.stmt: Use t = 200 partitionings by default and tune the sample size psi over {2^m : m = 1..8} (the same search space is used for the iForest/iNNE/IDK/ADERH baselines).
requirements.quote: For iForest, iNNE, IDK, ADERH and proposed methods, ψ ∈{2m, m = 1, 2, . . . , 8} and with default t = 200.

requirements.stmt: Follow the unsupervised contaminated-data protocol: fit on the whole dataset (normal + anomalous points), with no clean training set and no held-out split.
requirements.quote: our experiments assume access to the entire dataset containing both normal and anomalous instances during training

requirements.stmt: Run each experiment 5 times with different random partitions and report the average AUC-ROC.
requirements.quote: Each experiment is repeated 5 times and reported average results.

requirements.stmt: ISER-IF trains Isolation Forest on the phi-space representation Phi(x) rather than the raw features and inverts the score to S = 1 - 2^(-E(h(Phi(x)))/c(n)).
requirements.quote: we apply iForest to the transformed feature space Φ(x)

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with Area Under the ROC Curve only; scores must be oriented so that larger values mean more anomalous.
requirements.quote: We use Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC-ROC) as evaluation metrics.

requirements.stmt: Use the 20 published benchmark datasets from the PyOD and ODDS repositories listed in Table II, with the contamination rates given there.
requirements.quote: We conduct experiments on 20 real-world benchmark datasets from PyOD [32] and ODDS [33] repositories.

data.name: Ionosphere (ODDS benchmark copy)
data.how_to_get: ODDS outlier-detection dataset repository, https://shebuti.com/outlier-detection-datasets-odds (file Ionosphere.mat; 351 points, 32 features, 126 anomalies). Also bundled in the standard PyOD-style benchmark loaders.

data.name: The other 19 tabular benchmarks of Table II (Annthyroid, backdoor, breastw, celeba, fault, glass, Landsat, Lymphography, mnist, musk, pendigits, Pima, satellite, satimage-2, shuttle, skin, speech, vowels, WPBC)
data.how_to_get: Same ODDS repository (https://shebuti.com/outlier-detection-datasets-odds) and/or the PyOD repository data loaders; class labels are used only for computing AUC-ROC.

data.name: PyOD (toolbox for baselines LOF, iForest, ECOD, COPOD and data loading)
data.how_to_get: pip install pyod; paper reference [32] is 'PyOD: A python toolbox for scalable outlier detection'.

data.name: Synthetic two-moons visualisation set (300 points, 0.15 anomaly rate)
